name: Self-Training Classifier
analogy: Think of it as a new hire on a trading desk who has been told the market regime on only a handful of days. He labels the remaining days himself, one careful batch at a time, accepting only the days he is nearly sure about and learning from each batch before the next.

steps.title: Choose any classifier that reports its confidence
steps.description: Self-training is a wrapper placed around an ordinary classifier. The only requirement is that the classifier can say how sure it is, as a probability, because the process depends on that confidence.
steps.inExample: A random forest is chosen to label stretches of MNQ 5-minute bars as trending up, trending down or ranging.

steps.title: Train it on the labelled examples
steps.description: The classifier is fitted to the small set of examples with a known answer. This first version is the teacher for everything that follows.
steps.inExample: 400 stretches of 30 bars each have a hand-checked regime. The forest learns from these.

steps.title: Predict the unlabelled examples
steps.description: The classifier gives each unlabelled example a predicted class and a confidence in it. Many of these will be weak guesses.
steps.inExample: 8,000 unlabelled stretches each get a predicted regime and a confidence.

steps.title: Accept only the examples above the threshold
steps.description: Examples whose confidence clears a set threshold are accepted with the predicted class as their label. Everything below the threshold stays unlabelled for now.
steps.inExample: The threshold is 70 percent. In the first round, 900 stretches clear it and receive a regime label.

steps.title: Retrain on the enlarged set and repeat
steps.description: The classifier is fitted again on the real labels plus the accepted ones, then predicts the remaining unlabelled examples once more. The loop gives later rounds a stronger teacher than the first.
steps.inExample: Each retrain brings in a smaller batch of newly confident stretches than the round before.

steps.title: Stop when nothing qualifies or the round limit is reached
steps.description: The loop ends when no unlabelled example clears the threshold or when a maximum number of rounds is hit. The last classifier is the finished model and is then scored on later, held-out examples.
steps.inExample: After 5 rounds no new stretch clears 70 percent. The final forest labels a new stretch as trending up at 78 percent.

useFor.task: Regime labelling with few tagged examples
useFor.example: Tagging a few hundred stretches of MNQ bars as trending or ranging by hand and letting the process label thousands more.
Wrapping a tree ensemble or logistic model already in the pipeline, with no change to the model itself.

useFor.task: Building a bigger training set for a deeper model
useFor.example: Generating labels from a cheap forest to train a neural network that needs far more rows.
Labelling many unlabelled windows as double top, head-and-shoulders or no pattern after a small hand-labelled start.

avoidWhen: The first classifier is barely better than chance; its confident labels are then mostly wrong and each round reinforces them. Gather cleaner labels or use a graph-based method first.
You need an independent second opinion; a single classifier teaching itself repeats its own blind spots, so Co-Training or Tri-Training, which use several classifiers, are safer.

example.scenario: A researcher has 8,400 stretches of 30 five-minute MNQ bars. 400 have a hand-checked regime: trending up, trending down or ranging. The finished self-trained forest labels the stretch ending at 13:45.

input.summary: A stretch of 30 bars described by four summary numbers, plus the settings of the training loop.

fields.name: labelled stretches
fields.meaning: Stretches with a hand-checked regime that start the loop.

fields.name: acceptance threshold
fields.meaning: An unlabelled stretch is accepted only when the confidence in its predicted regime reaches this level.

fields.name: average directional index, 14 bars
fields.meaning: A trend-strength reading; above 25 is commonly read as trending.

fields.name: price change over the 30 bars
fields.meaning: How far price rose across the stretch.

fields.name: range width in average true ranges
fields.meaning: How wide the stretch's high-to-low range was, counted in units of the typical bar's travel.

fields.name: share of bars that closed up
fields.meaning: Two thirds of the stretch's bars closed above their open.

output.summary: A regime label for the stretch with a probability for each regime.

fields.name: regime label
fields.meaning: The regime with the highest probability.

fields.name: probability of trending up
fields.meaning: The classifier's confidence in the chosen regime.

fields.name: probability of ranging
fields.meaning: The classifier's confidence that the stretch was sideways.

fields.name: probability of trending down
fields.meaning: The classifier's confidence that the stretch was a down trend.

example.reading: 78 percent for trending up clears the 70 percent threshold, so this stretch would have been accepted as a label during the loop. Use the label as a regime tag for strategy choice, and check on later months that the tag is stable and not an artifact of the loop.
